Hi Oliver — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned on the Dedicated sizing/validation work: 

Summary of Atlas.ai targets we captured on the call:
- P95 generation latency target: <= 200 ms for 512-token responses (streaming enabled)
- Concurrent active requests: 40 (burst to 60)
- Sustained throughput: ~800 req/sec at average response size ~350 tokens (peak 1k req/sec)
- Streaming required for early token delivery (client-side UX depends on first-token <= 60 ms)
- Model family: you’ll be evaluating a 13B open model (quantized FP16/INT8 variants) with KV caching for chat histories

Immediate asks from your side:
1) Confirmation of the SLOs above (reply if any numbers differ)
2) A short test payload set and a sample prompt pattern (you mentioned an anonymized dataset — attachment ok)
3) A PO path/timeline if we provide a sizing recommendation and validation run

What we’ll do next (Redwood plan):
- Rafael and Dev will produce a Dedicated sizing recommendation comparing H100 vs A100 for your workload and propose reserved throughput (tokens/sec and requests/sec)
- We’ll scope a 1-week validation run (on-prem-like dedicated pool) to confirm p95 latency and streaming tail behavior with your payloads
- Deliverables: sizing doc, expected cost estimate, validation script + perf report

I attached the one-pager I promised and a blank perf-requirements spreadsheet — please fill the spreadsheet with any additional traffic patterns you want us to include.

Goal: get the sizing recommendation by Wednesday (8/11) and schedule the validation run the week of 8/16 if that works for you.

Hi all — high-level sizing notes based on the provided workload (13B quantized, avg 350 tokens, streaming):

Assumptions:
- Model: 13B quantized (int8/F16 mix) typical for chat use cases
- Average response length: 350 tokens; peak 600 tokens
- Effective token throughput is influenced by batching, KV cache hit rate, and sequence length distribution

Rough per-GPU throughput estimates (in dedicated serving environment, continuous batching, optimized kernels):
- H100 (80GB): ~1,200 - 1,800 requests/sec for short responses (~50 tokens) depending on batching; for longer responses (~350 tokens) think in tokens/sec: ~150k - 220k tokens/sec per GPU. In request/sec terms for 350 tokens avg: ~430 - 630 req/sec per GPU.
- A100 (80GB): ~900 - 1,400 requests/sec for short responses; tokens/sec ~110k - 160k. For 350 token avg: ~310 - 460 req/sec per GPU.

Latency guidance (with streaming enabled):
- First-token latency: dominated by decode startup + kernel launch. With streaming-first-token optimizations and small initial batch sizes we can hit ~40-60 ms on H100 and ~50-80 ms on A100 for typical prompts.
- P95 end-to-end (for 350 tokens): on a properly sized H100 pool with KV cache and request-aware batching we expect P95 in the 120-220 ms range depending on reserved throughput and burst headroom; A100 will be ~1.2x-1.6x slower generally (P95 ~160-320 ms).

Recommended reserved capacity (to meet Atlas targets: P95 <=200 ms at concurrency 40, streaming):
- Conservative recommendation: 2 x H100 (80GB) nodes reserved with autoscaling to add 1-2 additional H100s on burst. Rationale: At ~500 req/sec sustained equivalent (350 tokens avg) this gives comfortable headroom for concurrency and small batch sizes needed for streaming.
- If using A100: recommend 3 x A100 (80GB) reserved with autoscale for bursts.
- Tokens/sec reservation guidance: propose reserved baseline of 300k tokens/sec (covers ~850 req/sec at 350 tokens avg) with burst capacity up to 600k tokens/sec. This maps to the GPU counts above depending on model throughput assumptions.

Streaming + batching notes:
- To satisfy first-token <=60 ms we must limit initial micro-batch sizes for streaming requests; that reduces batching efficiency and increases per-token cost. We can mitigate by using KV caching for repeated chat histories and by applying request-level routing so that long-burst interactive sessions are placed on nodes optimized for low-latency streaming (smaller batch windows).
- Recommend a mixed pool: smaller low-latency pool (1-2 GPUs) for streaming-heavy sessions and a larger high-throughput pool for batch-heavy inference. Cross-pool routing/fallback can preserve SLOs during bursts.

Validation run timeline & artifacts:
- Timeline: 1 week (3 days to stage and baseline, 2-3 days of load tests and tuning, 1 day of report).
- Required from Atlas: model artifact (Docker image or model tar + quantization config), sample payloads (you provided — good), and a test account for integration.

Open items for Rafael to confirm cost delta (H100 vs A100) and for Aditya to validate these numbers against Redwood internal perf runs.

Happy to walk through numbers on a quick call.
